articles.title: Andrew Scott feels the Pressure as 'unsung hero' in WW2 thriller
articles.summary: The actor reveals how he approached playing James Stagg, the "chilly" meteorologist key to D-Day's success.
articles.body:
Andrew Scott says he loved the challenge of his latest acting role in the film Pressure, as the meteorologist key to the success of World War Two's D-Day - the largest seaborne invasion in history.

“Group Captain James Stagg may not have been the most charming person, but I think he had a huge amount of humility in the face of nature. And that's one of the themes I think of the film," Scott tells the BBC.

"He appeared to me to be an extraordinarily interesting cinematic character, as well as an unsung hero from history."

Stagg played a crucial advisory role when US General Dwight D Eisenhower invaded Normandy, laying the foundations for the Allied victory in World War Two.

"It was a wonderful part to play," he says, while painting a mixed picture of Stagg, calling him "very chilly", while also "forthright, direct, obsessed with weather - and not afraid to speak truth to power".

Stagg isn't a traditional war hero, something Scott clearly relished sinking his acting teeth into.

"I really enjoyed the way that Stagg was not interested in ingratiating himself with anybody," he told BBC Culture correspondent David Sillito, calling him "a real fish out of water in this situation".

The actor's other starring roles couldn't be more different, including romantic fantasy film All of Us Strangers, for which he was nominated for a Golden Globe, plus his memorable "hot priest" in TV's Fleabag and the menacing Jim Moriarty in Sherlock, for which he won a Bafta. His award-winning stage roles include Vanya and Present Laughter.

In Pressure, Stagg is thrown into a high-stakes furnace of egos. He has to work with a team of meteorologists who robustly and publicly disagree with each other.

Stagg "wasn't a particularly garrulous character" Scott says, which is partly why he was perhaps an unlikely hero.

"So many of the heroes in our own lives don't have that big swashbuckling moment," he says.

"And you know, a hero comes in all different shapes and sizes.

"I tried not to be afraid of the fact that perhaps, at the beginning, the audience might be like, 'Who is this guy?' And hopefully by the end we understand his motivations and his inner workings."

The actor is speaking to the BBC on board HMS Belfast, which led the opening bombardment for the D-Day landings , when tens of thousands of troops from the UK, the US, Canada and France attacked German forces on the coast of northern France on 6 June 1944.

"The stakes were so enormously high... they were all locked down, and they couldn't leave the place. Stagg's wife was very heavily pregnant at the time, so it was a very, very difficult time for him," Scott explains.

"It's completely unimaginable, the pressure that they would have been under, not just Stagg, but everybody in the building."

This of course explains the name of the film, which is based on the successful 2014 stage play by actor and writer David Haig.

The film also charts how Eisenhower had the good sense to pay heed to the experts around him.

Scott says although the film is about many things, it's chiefly about "the humility of leadership, and about the difference between power and expertise".

"Real experts have the humility to go, 'I don't know about that, but I am in a position of power, so I'm going to delegate this, and I'm gonna listen to what this person has to say'," he says.

The film's co-writer and director, Anthony Maras, employed his own weather experts for the film, including Martin Young, a former deputy chief of the UK's Met [Meteorology] Office , who'd spent 40 years studying the weather and more than 10 as its chief forecaster.

Young's long career also meant he had first-hand knowledge of processes, data and equipment Stagg would have used.

The film is nearly all set in the planning rooms for D-Day, and you see all of them working around the clock, while living on top of each other.

"There's a huge amount of wit in the film that I really enjoyed," Scott says, while adding: "I love films that are about work.

"These relationships are no less significant because they're work relationships, they're collegiate.

"And at the end of these extraordinary three days they shake hands with each other - he's not a hugger, that probably wasn't part of the culture then.

"But they nevertheless went through something absolutely enormous together, and they had enormous feelings towards each other - whether that was rage, admiration, intimidation or connection."

Scott also managed to use some previous experience of working on a film about D-Day to help with his performance.

"I've been very lucky. As a young actor, I was in the opening sequence of Saving Private Ryan [Steven Spielberg's Oscar-winning film which depicts the horror, fear and brutality facing troops landing at Normandy].

"I was there for that as a 19-year-old on the beach. So, of course, I have no sense of what the horrorism would have been like as a reality, but I certainly had an idea of how it would have looked visually because he stretched the camera for as long as the eye could see."

Scott is delighted that Pressure pays tribute not only to Stagg, but also references another unsung hero, Maureen Sweeney, who lived in Ireland and was the first to confirm any break in the weather, from her lighthouse in County Mayo.

"It's another story in itself actually," Scott adds.

"A big part of my family are from around those parts. So that was wonderful," the Irish actor adds.

Scott ends by saying why he was so drawn to the film, and Stagg in particular.

"I think there's something just very moving about a singular passion someone might get.

"Their imagination might get captured by the weather as a young man, and if you apply yourself to something and you become excellent at something, it serves a place in the world and serves a place in humanity.

"He quietly went back to his life and it's wonderful that we can pay tribute to him in this way all these years later. He's a movie hero."

Pressure is in UK and Irish cinemas from 9 September

articles.title: Michael Rapaport slams 'clown' Macklemore for anti-Israel performance
articles.summary: Michael Rapaport called Macklemore a "clown" after the rapper chanted "Free Palestine" and performed "Hind's Hall" at Ed Sheeran's MetLife shows.
articles.body: Michael Rapaport slammed Macklemore as a "clown" after the rapper brought his pro-Palestinian message to Ed Sheeran’s concert stage. Macklemore, 43, repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind's Hall" while opening for Sheeran, 35, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey during shows on Friday and Saturday nights. On Saturday, Rapaport, 56, who is Jewish and has become one of Hollywood’s most outspoken pro-Israel voices since Hamas' Oct. 7 attack, ripped Macklemore, born Benjamin Haggerty, in a blistering post on X. BLACK CROWES FACE BACKLASH AFTER CHRIS ROBINSON SHUTS DOWN U.S.A. CHANT AND CALLS FANS 'IGNORANT' 'Imagine going to see Ed Sheeran & this absolute no talent none singer non rapping non dancing clown Macklemore is opening & because he actually has no act or specific skill set he’s jumping around like dkc carrying on about a genocide that never happened in Gaza," Rapaport wrote, adding "This is a nightmare." In another critical post on X, the comedian questioned Sheeran’s decision to bring Macklemore on as an opening act. ED SHEERAN CONCERT WORKERS HOSPITALIZED AFTER FORKLIFT INCIDENT IN DETROIT: REPORT "So Ed Sheeran is ok with this p--- stain opening up for him? Sweet Ed Sheeran?" Rapaport wrote. Rapaport also reposted an article about the backlash to Macklemore's political messaging following the concerts, writing, "Calling this dude a ‘Rapper' is disrespectful to any actual ‘Rapper.’" ISRAEL, JEWS TARGETED WORLDWIDE AS WELL-FUNDED LEFTIST, ISLAMIST GROUPS JOIN FOR ‘NAKBA 78’ PROTESTS Fox News Digital has reached out to Macklemore and Sheeran's representatives for comment. In a video that Rapaport posted from the Friday night show, Macklemore, who wore a keffiyeh tied around his neck, was seen repeatedly chanting "Say free, free Palestine!" while music played as he walked around the stage and held up his microphone. Macklemore, who will be opening for Sheeran during the U.S. leg of the "Shape of You" singer's Loop Tour, also delivered a speech in which he said that he wanted to use stages across America to advocate for Palestine. ISRAELI PM NETANYAHU ARGUES PUBLIC OPINION SHIFT ON ISRAEL 'CORRELATES ALMOST 100%' TO SOCIAL MEDIA "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine," Macklemore said in a video shared on social media. "I said, ‘Free Palestine!’ I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them," he continued. "I have an 11-year-old daughter, her name is Sloan, she’s here tonight. And if any of you guys are parents, then you know that that love that you have for your kids cannot be put into words, right? I want to see her grow up, I want to see her go to school, to fall in love, to figure out meaning, purpose, joy, her existence on this planet. I want it to be the most beautiful possible." "And I think that every single human being that walks this earth deserves that exact same feeling. To know safety and peace before they know the sound of violence, to know the sound of laughter on a playground before planes and bombs, for parents to be able to say bye to their kids in the morning and not have to wonder if this is going to be the last time they kiss their child goodbye." "And if I let that fear I felt on the plane yesterday stop me from speaking my heart in order to keep my own comfort and the audience’s comfort, that is the day I no longer continue to be on stage," Macklemore added. "So, I say, ‘Free Palestine!’" RAGE AGAINST THE MACHINE'S TOM MORELLO FACES BACKLASH AFTER SINGING AT NYC ICE PROTEST RALLY Macklemore concluded his speech by calling for the freedom of other countries including America and blasting U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). "I say, free America, free Cuba to the Congo to Sudan to Iran, and all the people in America who have to live in fear because of this terrorist organization ICE," he said. HAMAS, HEZBOLLAH FLAGS FLY AT ANTI-ISRAEL PROTEST MINUTES AFTER MAMDANI CONDEMNS TERROR PLOT AGAINST JEWS Following his speech, Macklemore performed "Hind's Hall," a song inspired by the 2024 pro-Palestinian campus demonstrations," as footage from Gaza, pro-Palestinian protests, images of Israeli soldiers and pro-Palestinian messages were displayed on the stadium’s large screens. The title of the song refers to Hamilton Hall, the Columbia University building that pro-Palestinian students occupied in April 2024 and renamed in honor of a 6-year-old Palestinian girl killed in the Israel-Gaza war. The lyrics in "Hind's Hall" praised the anti-Israel encampments and protests on college campuses across the country and called out President Biden, the police and the music industry. RAPPER FACES $2.8M LAWSUIT AFTER AXING OPENING ACT FROM TOUR FOLLOWING HER POLITICAL RANT Macklemore also repeated his pro-Palestinian messaging during Sheeran’s second MetLife Stadium show Saturday night, again calling for "Free Palestine" and performing his protest song "Hind’s Hall." While some audience members cheered Macklemore's comments and joined the "Free Palestine" chant, the rapper's performance was met with backlash from other attendees. One concertgoer said on X that he brought his wife and two daughters to Friday’s show as longtime Sheeran fans, but left disappointed after Macklemore’s set turned political. The fan said his daughters looked "completely confused" when Macklemore began chanting "Free Palestine," adding that he had taken them to "an Ed Sheeran concert, not to have an opening act lecture them about Middle East politics." He said his family left their seats during Macklemore’s performance and returned after the rapper finished, praising Sheeran’s show as "phenomenal" but criticizing the singer for allowing Macklemore to perform again Saturday. "Friday might have been Macklemore’s decision. Saturday was yours," the concertgoer wrote, adding, "Tonight, you lost four of them. And I suspect plenty more." Another concertgoer said he attended Saturday’s show in a company suite with 35 other people and was "embarrassed" and "shocked" by Macklemore’s set. The attendee said he had "always been a Macklemore fan," but after the rapper’s "political stunt," he could no longer support him or his music. "When you go WOKE, you have to be prepared to lose fans," he wrote. The concertgoer also denounced Sheeran for allowing Macklemore to return to the stage Saturday after the backlash from the previous night. "After it happened on Friday, it should have immediately been stopped," he wrote, adding that he went to the show to hear "amazing music," not "Free Palestine" rants. Two other concertgoers told Ynet, the English edition of Israel's largest new website, that they were unfamiliar with Macklemore before the show and unaware that he would be performing. "We only found out there and we were in shock. It was really horrifying," they said. "We immediately thought about everything our people have been through and how even when we’re abroad we still have to feel this antisemitism," they continued. "It was even harder because friends of ours were killed in the war and murdered at Nova. It was like a knife in the heart to hear him sing that way and hear people cheering." The concertgoers said that some of the members in their group began crying and left the show before Sheeran's performance. However, some social media users praised Macklemore for speaking up and expressed their support for the rapper's message. "Huge respect for Ed Sheeran, but seeing Macklemore use his voice for Palestine made this moment mean so much more," one fan wrote on Instagram. "Respect to every artist who refuses to stay silent and uses their platform to speak up for humanity. Macklemore, we hear you." "LOVE Macklemore, and good on him using his platform to speak out….his messaging is always spot on. Peace," another agreed. "Free free Palestine. Love to Macklemore. Stay true," one fan chimed in. "this was from last night!! I hope you get to perform this again tonight too!" a fan wrote alongside a clip from Macklemore's set. "So happy we get to witness such history!" one fan commented. "Honestly I loved this part of the concert !" another wrote. "Music has always been a vital platform for human rights advocacy, not just mindless escape," wrote one X user. "Calling for peace, safety, and equality for Palestinians, Congolese, and Sudanese isn't antisemitic—it's pro-humanity. Macklemore explicitly stands for collective liberation and love." "Art has always been political, why are you annoyed at an artist giving context to a song he released about the current state of the world you live in?" another fan commented on X. "Also, he was an opener, they could’ve just skipped his set! Although I hope Macklemore sings it louder next time!" "This was an Ed Sheeran concert – not a political rally, not a protest, and not an activist event," the petition read. "The issue is not whether Macklemore has the right to hold political views. The question is where the line should be drawn when an opening act uses a global concert platform to advance a one-sided political agenda." Macklemore has been outspoken in his support for Palestinians since the start of the Israel-Hamas war. In November 2023, Macklemore spoke at a pro-Palestinian rally in Washington, D.C., where he said, "I don’t know enough. But I know enough that this is a genocide." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? articles.title: Barbara Eden, 95, says she’s ‘okay’ after last-minute cancelation of festival appearance
articles.summary: Barbara Eden reassured fans after a "sudden illness" forced her to miss the Cinecon Classic Film Festival, revealing a new medication's side effects.
articles.body: Barbara Eden sparked concern among fans after abruptly dropping out of a Los Angeles film festival due to what was described as a "sudden illness," but the 95-year-old actress later shared a reassuring update on social media. The "I Dream of Jeannie" star was set to be honored during the Cinecon Classic Film Festival at the Landmark Nuart Theatre on Saturday but pulled out shortly before the event was scheduled to begin. "We’re sorry to share that, due to a sudden illness, Barbara Eden will no longer be able to appear in person at Cinecon tonight," festival organizers announced in a Facebook post on Saturday. ROD STEWART CALLED 'TONE-DEAF' FOR ATTENDING WORLD CUP GAME A DAY CANCELING CONCERT DUE TO HEALTH ISSUES "Barbara is deeply regretful that she had to cancel at the last minute, as she had been very much looking forward to seeing everyone and celebrating with us," they continued. "We know how many of you were excited to welcome Barbara. We appreciate your understanding and join you in sending her our best wishes for a speedy recovery," they added. 'YOU'RE SO VAIN' SINGER CARLY SIMON SAYS PARKINSON'S AND CANCER DIAGNOSES KEPT HER FROM PUBLIC EYE Eden later took to Instagram to clarify the circumstances around her absence and update fans on her condition. "It’s okay everyone! I’m okay!" she wrote alongside a photo in which she was seen standing in front of a painting and smiling. "Oh, my goodness there has been a bit of miscommunication," Eden continued. "I’m not suffering from an illness; my doctor very recently prescribed a brand-new medication that turned out to have some nasty side effects. Due to the discomfort, my doctor ordered me to remain at home until it can be sorted out." MAYIM BIALIK DETAILS 'NIGHTMARE' AFTER ONE INJECTION OF GLP-1 DRUG LED TO WEEKS OF DEBILITATING SIDE EFFECTS "What awful timing for this to happen! My deepest appreciation to everyone for the concern," she added. "This is just a speedbump! I expect to be out and about as soon as I’m given the go-ahead!" "Again, my love and thanks to everyone for all the concern," she concluded. Cinecon is a classic film festival in Los Angeles that celebrates vintage movies, rare screenings and stars from Hollywood’s Golden Age. This year’s Cinecon marked the festival’s 62nd edition. CURATORS AT LIBRARY OF CONGRESS DISCOVER LOST FILM BY LEGENDARY CINEMA PIONEER AFTER SPOTTING 'SUBTLE CLUE' Eden was scheduled to receive the Cinecon Legacy Award alongside a screening of her 1961 film "All Hands on Deck." She had been expected to introduce the movie with her co-star Pat Boone, who later accepted the Cinecon Legacy Award on her behalf. The Cinecon Legacy Award is an honor given by the Cinecon Classic Film Festival to entertainment professionals for their lifetime achievements and contributions to the motion picture and entertainment industries. RICK MORANIS, CAMERON DIAZ AND LINDSAY LOHAN AMONG STARS WHO LEFT FAME BEHIND BEFORE RETURNING TO HOLLYWOOD Eden is best known for starring as Jeannie opposite Larry Hagman in the classic NBC sitcom "I Dream of Jeannie," which ran from 1965 to 1970 and made her one of television’s most recognizable stars. The actress's career has spanned more than seven decades across film, TV and theater. Her film credits include "Flaming Star" opposite Elvis Presley, "Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea" and "Harper Valley P.T.A." and she has also starred in the hit TV shows "Dallas" and "Sabrina the Teenage Witch." articles.title: En 2025, Leonardo Di Caprio compró una isla en Chile para que no fuera deforestada: ahora quiere donarla al gobierno para hacer un parque nacional
articles.standfirst: El actor dedica gran parte de su tiempo fuera del cine a trabajos relacionados con el cuidado de la naturaleza
articles.summary: El actor dedica gran parte de su tiempo fuera del cine a trabajos relacionados con el cuidado de la naturaleza
articles.body: En el archipiélago Chiloé, perteneciente a Chile, se encuentra la isla Guafo, un pequeño trozo de tierra, de solo 197 kilómetros cuadrados, donde viven únicamente cuatro personas. Un lugar del mundo que, además tiene dueño: Leonardo DiCaprio, el actor compró la isla en 2025, después de estar a la venta desde el año 2020. Sin embargo, el actor no la adquirió para hacer lo que cualquier famoso haría: una isla privada en la que hacer fiestas. En el caso del intérprete ganador de un Oscar la razón fue para proteger la biodiversidad del lugar, es decir, evitar la minería de carbón y la tala masiva. Su asociación, Re:wild, de la que es cofundador, es la que se encargó de comprar la isla, con la idea de convertirla en un parque nacional. Se le ha bautizado como ‘la pequeña Galápagos’, situada en el sur de Chile, con el propósito de que llegue a ser un santuario. Lo que más llama la atención del lugar son sus bosques, repletos de fardelas negras, o sus aguas, donde pueden verse ballenas azules y sei, ambas en peligro de extinción. Ahora, la intención es ceder la propiedad al Gobierno chileno, pero no es tan fácil como parece. La controversia surge de las quejas de las comunidades mapuche-williche de Quellón, denunciando que no han contado con ellos en la compra inicial, enterándose por los medios de comunicación. Ahora, estos líderes indígenas, unidos en el proyecto 'Wafo Wapi', han comenzado a negociar con Re:wild y WWF Chile, tratando de mantener los derechos territoriales de los pueblos originarios. Y es que, en 2016, DiCaprio ya demostró estar muy comprometido con el cuidado del medioambiente, después de estrenar el documental ‘Before the Flood’, junto a National Geographic. En él, el actor graba diferentes encuentros con científicos, activistas y líderes mundiales para debatir sobre el cambio climático, los peligros que esto supone y las soluciones que puede haber en torno a ello.

articles.title: ‘Widow’s Bay’ dominates with 8 Emmys at early ceremony, ‘The Pitt’ takes 4
articles.summary: Widow’s Bay” ran away with eight early Emmys for its debut season Sunday at a ceremony eight days before the main awards show and telecast, while “The Pitt” had a strong second-year showing with four of its own.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — “Widow’s Bay” ran away with eight early Emmys for its debut season Sunday at a ceremony eight days before the main awards show and telecast, while “The Pitt” had a strong second-year showing with four of its own, and Rob Reiner posthumously won an acting Emmy nearly nine months after his killing. “DTF St. Louis” won big with six awards in the limited series categories, with co-stars and veteran actors David Harbour and Linda Cardellini both becoming first-time Emmy winners. “Widow’s Bay,” the Apple TV horror comedy with Matthew Rhys as the mayor of a small New England town dealing with a centuries-old curse, won categories including cinematography, sound, music and production design. Betty Gilpin won best guest actress in a comedy for her role on the show, and read a rapid-fire comic poem as her acceptance speech. It included the lines “our business is stupid, but actors are the bomb” and “let’s all lean more toward Sam Shepard and less toward Sam Altman.” ‘The Pitt’ has strong second-year showing HBO Max’s day-in-the-life medical series “The Pitt” — the year’s top nominee with 25 and the reigning best drama winner for its first season — had wins Sunday in categories including prosthetic makeup and best guest actor in a drama for 73-year-old first-time nominee Ernest Harden Jr. Harden, who won for portraying the last days of Louie Cloverfield, the emergency room’s constant presence and constantly struggling alcoholic on “The Pitt,” wept when his name was called. “I am just on cloud 25,” he said backstage at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. “I’m not saying it’s a complete surprise because ‘The Pitt’ is such a powerful show to come from, but just to get it in your hands is unreal.” Harden’s first speaking role was in the 1975 Robert Redford-Faye Dunaway thriller “Three Days of the Condor” and he had a three-season role on the sitcom “The Jeffersons” in the 1970s, but has acted for decades without awards recognition. Singer-songwriter Andrew Bird and Gavin Brivik won for original music and lyrics for a song they wrote about the character. “It’s not a music-heavy show,” Bird said backstage. “But they gave us a beautiful moment with a character that we love.” Rebranding the Creative Arts Emmys and adding some star power The Television Academy hands out well over 100 primetime Emmys, and most of them are being presented this weekend in a pair of ceremonies. They were previously known as the Creative Arts Emmys but have now been rebranded as simply the first two nights of the 78th Emmy Awards. The weekend’s awards primarily go to behind-the-scenes crew members, but they include the guest-acting awards that tend to go to bigger names. And the shows’ star power got a boost when five categories normally on the main telecast were bumped to the earlier weekend, among them best supporting actor in a limited series, won by Harbour in his third nomination, and best supporting actress in a limited series, won by Linda Cardellini in her fourth nomination in an elite TV career that included roles on “Freaks and Geeks” and “Mad Men.” “Thank you to everybody who along the way through the years helped me get to this moment of a real dream come true,” Cardellini said from the stage, through tears. Rob Reiner gets a somber ovation At a ceremony that otherwise moved at a blazing-fast clip with a breezy mood, a long, thoughtful ovation came when Reiner was announced as best guest actor in a comedy for his work on “The Bear.” Reiner’s friend and fellow “Bear” guest star Jamie Lee Curtis was among those in the crowd paying him tribute. Reiner was killed along with his wife Michele Singer Reiner in December, and their son, who has pleaded not guilty, has been charged with stabbing them to death. His win came about 50 years after winning two Emmy Awards for his acting on “All in the Family.” Saturday and Sunday’s ceremonies will be edited together to air Sept. 12 on FXX and stream on Hulu the following day. The primetime Sept. 14 ceremony, also at the Peacock Theater and hosted by Mariska Hargitay, will air live on NBC and stream live on Peacock. Both “Widow’s Bay” and “The Pitt” can add up to six more Emmys to their totals on that final night. “Pluribus,” another Apple TV Emmy rookie from “Breaking Bad” creator Vince Gilligan that could challenge “The Pitt” in the top drama categories, won four trophies Sunday night including editing, production design and sound mixing. Shailene Woodley and a canceled ‘Spider-Noir’ are also winners Shailene Woodley won best guest actress in a drama for her role on “Paradise.” It was her first Emmy. “Spider-Noir,” the Nicolas Cage series which was canceled after one season last week by Amazon Prime Video, won five Emmys, including visual effects and stunts. Hargitay was among this weekend’s winners, getting two Emmys for the documentary she directed about her mother, Jayne Mansfield, “My Mom Jayne,” to go with the best actress in a drama Emmy she won in 2006 for “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.” And Bad Bunny won his first career Emmy Award for his Super Bowl halftime show, which took seven trophies at the first of the weekend’s ceremonies on Saturday.

articles.body: TRIGGER WARNING: This article contains mention of death.Malayali singer Nisar Wayanad passed away at a hospital in Dubai on Saturday evening. The singer was due to perform at an event in Ajman just hours before his death, as reported by Gulf News.Born Nissar Aroth Ibrahim, the 44-year-old singer was widely recognised for his voice, which closely resembled that of popular Bollywood playback singer Udit Narayan. He was popularly known by his stage name, Nisar Wayanad. The name also reflected his roots in Wayanad, Kerala.Nisar Wayanad had been a familiar name among Malayali communities in the UAE. He regularly performed at musical programmes and community events in Dubai. His ability to recreate Udit Narayan's voice became one of the defining aspects of his stage performances. He is survived by his wife and two daughters.Nisar Wayanad was hospitalised after high feverAs reported by Gulf News website, according to Nisar Wayanad's friends in Dubai, the singer developed a high fever on Saturday afternoon. He was subsequently taken to a hospital in Dubai for treatment. Reports stated that the death notification listed “acidosis” as the direct cause of death. His passing occurred on the same day he was expected to perform in Ajman.Nisar Wayanad had admired Udit NarayanNisar Wayanad had never hidden his admiration for Udit Narayan. His love for the veteran playback singer was also evident from an old social media post.In the post, Nisar Wayanad recalled the moment he finally met Udit Narayan after waiting for two decades.“A dream I’ve held onto for so many years has finally come true… My love for Udit Narayan sir’s songs is beyond words.From as far back as I can remember, I’ve been his biggest fan…I waited 20 years for this moment—to meet him in person and give him a heartfelt hug/kiss… Today, I am truly happy.A moment I will cherish forever…”Nisar Wayanad performed across DubaiNisar Wayanad was often introduced as a Mappilapattu singer. However, his musical repertoire was broader than the traditional folk genre from Kerala.He performed songs in different styles and was especially known for Bollywood numbers. His resemblance to Udit Narayan's voice helped him stand out during live shows.Afsal remembers Nisar Wayanad as a dear friendFollowing the news of his death, Malayalam playback singer Afsal paid tribute to Nisar Wayanad on social media. Afsal remembered him as a “dear friend”.Nisar Wayanad's career was not restricted to stage performances. He had also explored opportunities in the film industry and lent his voice to a Kannada film. articles.summary: El cantante justificó su nuevo peinado durante un concierto en Granada
articles.body: Dani Martín finalizó su gira ‘25 P*ut*s años’ este fin de semana en Granada. Si bien, la noticia no está en el adiós momentáneo del artista de los escenarios, sino en su cambio de look. Si a algo nos tiene acostumbrados el madrileño desde sus primeros pasos como vocalista de ‘El canto del loco’ ha sido a sus innumerables cambios de peinado. Le hemos visto de todas las maneras posibles: rubio platino, rapado, rosa, más largo, más corto, con cresta... Durante su show en Granada sorprendió a todos los asistentes con su nuevo ‘look’ provocado por un pequeño accidente y no porque al cantante le apeteciera raparse la cabeza. Así lo contó el propio artista justo antes de interpretar Peter Pan, una de las canciones más míticas de la banda. Quizá aprovechó este momento en el que nos evoca a ser niños siempre, para explicar el motivo de su rapado. “Me desvelé y cogí la máquina de afeitar y creía que tenía el peine puesto en la máquina. Hice así (se pasa la mano por la cabeza) y no lo tenía puesto. Tenía el pelo rubio... y me afeité. Así estoy. Me van a disculpar, con 49 años aparecer aquí, de esta guisa, como un muchacho de 14... Fresquito para el verano”, explicaba el madrileño cuando bajó a pista entre sus seguidores. Como era de esperar y, con todo lo que rodea a Dani Martín, poco tardó el vídeo del momento en hacerse viral. Su nuevo peinado ha sido bien acogido por sus seguidores que le recuerdan a esa etapa del cantante en los primeros años de ‘El Canto del Loco’ en los que tenía la cabeza rapada. "Fresquito si vas a estar desde luego, con estas calores"; "Ay Dani, qué te has hecho"; "Muero de amor con él". articles.title: Así le ha cambiado la vida a Laura Moure, de 'La Ruleta de la suerte': "Mi nueva realidad"
articles.standfirst: La copresentadora ha sido madre de una niña
articles.summary: La copresentadora ha sido madre de una niña
articles.body: Laura Moure atraviesa un momento radical de cambio en su vida. De los que marcan de verdad. Hace pocos días ha sido madre y entra de lleno en otra dimensión. Con evidentes cambios. La copresentadora de 'La Ruleta de la Suerte' daba a luz a su primera hija. Se llama Zoe y es fruto de su relación con su pareja, Kiko Chica. Se ha dado a conocer estos días que nació el pasado 2 de septiembre. De hecho, ya el pasado marzo la propia Laura anunció que estaba embarazada y que el bebé llegaría para agosto, pero se ha retrasado brevemente. "Os presento a la pequeña Zoe. Está creciendo de maravilla!! En agosto la tendré entre mis brazos por fin!!!", señalaba meses atrás. Y por fin ha llegado el momento. La azafata y copresentadora de 'La ruleta de la suerte' lleva mucho tiempo en el programa con Jorge Fernández. Suma la friolera de más de 11 años junto al presentador vasco lo que les ha convertido en una de las parejas más estables del mundo de la televisión con lo difícil que es este asunto. De hecho, se incorporó al programa a principios de 2015 en sustitución de Paloma López y desde entonces supo crecer en el mismo y asentarse como un rostro habitual. Moure se encarga de desvelar las letras que aparecen sombreadas en el panel cuando un concursante las elige. Además, añade ritmo y ánimo al concurso. Cada vez ha ido ganando un poco de mayor presencia en el mismo bajo el acompañamiento a Jorge Fernández. Ya es un rostro reconocido y habitual. Forman un buen tándem profesional. Laura Moure también ha tenido una faceta como actriz y, por el momento, ha participado en series tan famosas como 'Hospital Central' o 'Al filo de la ley', además de haber compartido escaleta con Álex González en la película 'Combustión'.

articles.summary: JD Vance's mother Beverly defended Usha Vance on Tomi Lahren's show after online critics mocked the second lady's $8 Old Navy maternity dress.
